questions.title: The bony rim above the orbit
questions.question: What structure is located immediately above the orbit when viewed in norma frontalis?

explanations.A: Correct. Viewed from the front (norma frontalis), the bony rim directly above each orbit is the supraorbital margin. It is formed by the frontal bone and carries the supraorbital notch or foramen for the supraorbital nerve and vessels. Its counterpart, the infraorbital margin, sits on the opposite (inferior) side of the same orbit.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The infraorbital margin is the corresponding rim BELOW the orbit, formed mainly by the maxilla with a zygomatic contribution — the opposite side of the orbit from the one asked about.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The frontal eminence is a rounded prominence higher up on the forehead, a separate landmark from the sharp orbital rim itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The zygomatic process is a separate projection of the frontal bone that forms part of the lateral orbital margin, not the superior margin.

questions.learning_objective: Locate the supraorbital margin above the orbit and distinguish it from the infraorbital margin and nearby landmarks.
